title: Spike-adaptive probe-and-rollback controller for model fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: During transient traffic spikes we observe short-lived 429 bursts and elevated tail latency that trigger aggressive fallback to lower-capacity model variants, causing unnecessary quality regressions for customers. Goal: Implement a spike-adaptive probe-and-rollback controller that (1) distinguishes transient spikes from sustained degradation using short-window pattern analysis, (2) gates automatic fallback decisions behind a lightweight prober that validates variant health before cutting over, and (3) supports automatic rollback with hysteresis and cooldown windows to avoid flip-flopping. This ticket covers design, implementation, telemetry, and an initial canary rollout for host-level and regional routing policies.
background: Current fallback logic is largely threshold-based (429/timeouts/error-rate) with simple rate-limited circuit breakers. We lack a compact probe step that can validate variant correctness under real traffic with minimal user-visible latency impact. Consequence: noisy signals can cause model-quality regressions and tenant churn.
design_notes: Core pieces: (a) Spike detector: short sliding window (10s) spike score + longer window (5m) baseline to classify spike vs sustained; (b) Probe executor: issue low-rate synchronous probes to candidate variant using live request replication and lightweight input sampling; (c) Decision FSM: combine probe success rate, probe latency, and primary route error profile to decide fallback, with configurable hysteresis and gradual ramp; (d) Rollback controller: cooldown double-backoff and minimum-stability interval before rollback. All knobs surfaced via routing config and Console UI and exposed to Dedicated private control plane via rollout policies.
implementation_plan: 1) Add spike-detector library to routing service (C++/Rust module) with feature flag. 2) Implement probe executor that can be enabled per-tenant; probes are tagged and counted separately in telemetry. 3) Extend circuit-breaker state-machine with new states: PROBING, STAGED_FAILOVER, LOCKED_COOLDOWN. 4) Wire new decision signals into existing smart-router policy engine and introduce a compact API for model-variant probe evaluation. 5) Create migration toggle and default conservative config for hosted tier. 6) Instrument dashboards and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Spike detector correctly classifies synthetic traffic patterns (unit + integration tests covering spike vs sustained >95% accuracy)
Probes can be executed at <1% overhead for a high-throughput route (benchmarked on dedicated pool)
Automatic fallback only triggers after probe pass threshold or sustained degradation window (configurable)
Rollback after false-positive fallback completes without further model-quality regressions in canary region over 30 minutes
New metrics emitted: probe_success_rate, probe_latency_p50/p95, spike_score, staged_failover_count, rollback_count
No customer-facing 5xx increases detected during canary (compare 10m window pre/post)
Configurable knobs exposed in Console and available via API for Dedicated/Private
test_plan: Unit tests for spike detector logic with deterministic time windows
Integration test that injects 429/timeouts and verifies probe behavior and decision FSM transitions
Load test to validate probe overhead at scale in a staging cluster identical to production pool
Canary rollout in a single region for customers on staged tier with manual monitoring for 48h
Chaos run: intermittently increase upstream latency and confirm controller prefers probes over immediate fallback when spike classifier fires
risks: Probe traffic could itself amplify load if poorly tuned — mitigated by strict max-probe-rate and sampling
False negatives: probe may succeed while production path still degrades due to path-specific throttles; require probe routing to mirror production path as closely as possible
Complexity of new FSM increases maintenance burden for on-call — add compact state dump to telemetry and page-runbook updates
Cross-tenant interaction risk in shared pools — default probes to tenant-scoped and disable cross-tenant replication
